Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office

PUBLIC COMMENTS ON AGENDA ITEMS
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with
another person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor
and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.
Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours
before a meeting. Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.
This Agenda includes items considered by the City Council acting on behalf of the Successor
Agency of the former Monterey Park Redevelopment Agency which dissolved February 1, 2012.
Successor Agency matters will include the notation of “SA” next to the Agenda Item Number.

1.  EMERGENCY REPAIR/REPLACEMENT OF WASTEWATER MAIN AND WATER
  MAIN IN ALLEY EAST OF ATLANTIC BLVD BETWEEN EL MERCADO AVENUE
  AND EL PORTAL PLACE
  It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1)  Adopt a resolution declaring an emergency and authorizing contracting without
  the need for bidding pursuant to Public Contracts Code §§ 20168 and 22050;
  (2)  Authorize the City Manager to (a) execute a public works contract between the
  City of Monterey Park and a qualified contractor(s), for wastewater main, water
  main, and asphalt repairs in the alley east of Atlantic Blvd. between El Mercado
  and El Portal, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and (b) Appropriate funds
  from the Wastewater and Water Capital accounts from the current fiscal year
  budget to cover the cost of these repairs;
  (3)  Authorize the Director of Public Works to approve change orders and contingency
  as appropriate up to 15% of the contract amount for this project; and
  (4)  Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
  The emergency and extended repairs are categorically exempt from the requirements of
  the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to 14 California Code of
  Regulations § 15269 (emergency repair to this public facility is necessary to maintain
  service essential to the public, health and welfare) and § 15301 (Existing Facilities). The
  extended repairs would result in minor alterations to existing public facilities involving no
  significant expansion of the existing use. The project is not anticipated to have any
  significant impacts with regard to traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality. There are
  adequate utilities and public services to serve the project.

SUBJEGT:  Emergency Repair/Replacement of Wastewater Main and Water Main
  in Alley East of Atlantic Blvd between El Mercado Avenue and El Portal
  Place

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council:
  1. Adopt a resolution declaring an emergency and authorizing contracting without the
  need for bidding pursuant to Public Contracts Code SS 20168 and 22050;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to (a) execute a public works contract between the
  City of Monterey Park and a qualified contractor(s), for wastewater main, water
  main, and asphalt repairs in the alley east of Atlantic Blvd. between El Mercado
  and El Portal, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and (b) Appropriate funds
  from the Wastewater and Water Capital accounts from the current fiscal year
  budget to cover the cost of these repairs;
  3. Authorize the Director of Public Works to approve change orders and contingency
  as appropriate up to 15o/o of the contract amount for this project; and
  4. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

CEQA (California Environmental Qualitv Act):

The emergency and extended repairs are categorically exempt from the requirements of
the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to 14 California Code of
Regulations S 15269 (emergency repair to this public facility is necessary to maintain
service essential to the public, health and welfare) and S 15301 (Existing Facilities). The
extended repairs would result in minor alterations to existing public facilities involving no
significant expansion of the existing use. The project is not anticipated to have any
significant impacts with regard to traffic, noise, air quality, or water quality. There are
adequate utilities and public services to serve the project.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

A wastewater main collapse occurring on or about June 12, 2019 blocked wastewater
flows from being conveyed. Currently, temporary pumping operations have been set up
to keep local businesses and residents in service. Staff is meeting with several
contractors to obiain bids to perform emergency wastewater anci water main repairs or

replacement to reestablish wastewater flows and eliminate water leaks, which compound
the wastewater issues.

BACKGROUND:

On or about June 12,2019 an 8-inch cement concrete wastewater main, built in 1933,
collapsed in several areas within the alley east of South Atlantic Blvd between El
Mercado Avenue and El Portal Place. ln addition to the age of the wastewater main,
multiple water leaks from the adjacent 4-inch cast iron water main may have caused the
wastewater collapse or compounded the issues. Currently, wastewater flows are being
blocked and therefore temporary bypass of the flows are occurring through the operation
of two pumps, in order to keep over 20 businesses, such as several restaurants, and
residents with wastewater service.

Additionally, the wastewater main collapse and water main leaks resulted in extensive
infrastructure damage besides the mains themselves such as the underlying alley
roadway bed, which could potentially lead to sink holes. The alley serves as the main
access for deliveries to the businesses served by these wastewater and water mains and
it is therefore important that it is structurally sound.

The City does not yet have a firm dollar figure or contractor for this project. While it is an
emergency, and the City caused temporary measures to be installed to ensure continued
wastewater service pending a permanent solution, the City is seeking the lowest dollar
figure with the best contractor. The Engineer's estimate for this project is in the $500,000
range; there are approximately 600-750 linear that must be excavated and constructed.

There are current discussions with four different qualified contractors for this work. The
City will select the best contractor for the lowest price; work is anticipated to begin next
week.

FISCAL IMPACT:

The Project will be paid for using funds from the Wastewater and Capital funds and staff
will update City Council as soon as contract has been awarded.

  DECLARATION OF EMERGENCY

The City Manager finds:

  That conditions of extreme peril to the safety of persons and property have
arisen within the City of Monterey Park, as a result of a sewer main break and
damage to the alley adjacent to S Atlantic Blvd between El Mercado Avenue and
El Portal Place, commencing on or about June 12, 2019 at 6:00 a.m.

  These conditions of extreme peril warrant and necessitate the
proclamation of the existence of a local emergency.

  Accordingly, pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code S 2.52.060(aX1),
a local emergency is proclaimed to exist within the City of Monterey Park. This
action witl be taken to the City Council for confirmation within seven days.

  Scott Haberle, Acting City Manager
